items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: I remember thinking about like Ellington used to write not for a tenor sax, he’d write for Ben Webster.

ctx.x: Yeah. I remember thinking about like Ellington used to write not for a tenor sax, he’d write for Ben Webster.

Yeah, yeah. Like I had to write something for the horns, I knew what Maceo could do. I knew what Russell Crimes could do and I knew what Ike Oakley could do. I knew what each player could do. So I wouldn’t write over their heads, I wouldn’t write under their heads either. I’d let Maceo take the lead on some things, you know, over the trumpets you know. Because he was a far better musician than Russell Crimes. See he was a good musician but he couldn’t play certain notes you know. So yeah I did. I did write for…
